note: PRD-01 requirement 6 — past CARD_RENDER_CAP the board must SAY it truncated. Read this report as a REGISTER comparison and nothing stronger: the mock has no board cap line at all, so the design side here is the TABLE surface, whose .sft-cap footer is the design's one and only "this view is truncated, and says so" element ("Showing 8 of 1284 rows · 6 of 6 columns · render cap 200"). Rows below therefore answer "does the live cap line read like the design's cap register?", not "does it match a board cap line the design specified" — the design specified none. The badge pair is included because it is the other half of the same question: the badge states the TRUE total while the cap line states how much of it is painted.

elements.label: cap.line
elements.note: Design register: mono 10px on --mut2, --ink2 ground, top hairline, 7px 12px padding, 13px gap. Live composes an inline 12px sans on --color-text-muted with no ground and no border.

elements.label: cap.badge
elements.note: Both state the true total (design "8 of 1284 rows", live "260 cards") rather than the painted slice — which is the behaviour PRD-01 wants; only the register is in question.

elements.label: cap.card
elements.note: Context anchor, so a cap-line delta can be read against the card it sits in.

unmapped.why: The design state is the table surface only because of its cap footer. Its grid is the subject of a different piece of work (the shared table language) and is deliberately not anchored here — this file must not turn into a table-parity report by accident.
